{{Short description|Concept in combinatorial game theory}}
In [[combinatorial game theory]], '''up''', written as <math>\uparrow</math>, is the value of the game where Left can only move to a [[zero game]], while Right can only move to a [[Star (game theory)|star game]]. It is greater than [[0|zero]] and less than all [[Positive real numbers|positive numbers]], hence it is an [[infinitesimal]]. <math>\uparrow</math> may be represented by the [[Surreal number|surreal form]]<math display="block">\uparrow=\{0\mid* \}.</math>Because <math>\uparrow>0</math>, Left always wins a game with value <math>\uparrow</math>. Its [[additive inverse]], down, written as <math>\downarrow</math>, may be represented as<math display="block">\downarrow=\{*\mid 0\}.</math>Similarly, <math>\downarrow</math> is less than zero and greater than all [[Negative number|negative numbers]].

<math>\uparrow</math> and <math>\downarrow</math> are equivalent to <math>+_0</math> and <math>-_0</math>, [[Tiny and miny|tiny-0 and miny-0]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last1=Albert |first1=Michael Henry |title=Lessons in play: an introduction to combinatorial game theory |last2=Nowakowski |first2=Richard J. |last3=Wolfe |first3=David |date=2007 |publisher=AK Peters |isbn=978-1-56881-277-9 |location=Wellesley, Mass}}</ref>

== Value-<math>\uparrow</math> games ==

=== Hackenbush ===
[[File:Blue Flower in Hackenbush.png|thumb|A 1-petaled blue flower, often called a delphinium. It has value <math>\uparrow+*</math>.]]
In [[Hackenbush]], a 1-petaled delphinium, that is, a blue edge on top of a green edge, has value <math>\{0,*\mid0 \}=\uparrow+*</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=Berlekamp |first1=Elwyn R. |title=Winning ways for your mathematical plays |last2=Conway |first2=John Horton |last3=Guy |first3=Richard K. |date=2001 |publisher=A.K. Peters |isbn=978-1-56881-130-7 |edition=2nd |location=Natick (Mass.)}}</ref> Hence, a green edge along with a 1-petaled delphinium has value <math>\uparrow+*+*=\uparrow</math>.

=== Col ===
Because a [[Col (game)|Col]] position can have only values <math>z</math> or <math>z+*</math> for some number <math>z</math>,<ref name=":0" /> no Col position can have value <math>\uparrow</math>.

=== Toads and Frogs ===
In [[Toads and Frogs]], <math>\uparrow</math> may be represented by the position<ref name=":0" /> <math display="block">T\square TFF=\{\square TTFF\mid TFT\square F\}=\{0\mid\{TF\square TF\mid TFTF\square\}\}=\{0\mid\{0\mid0\}\}=\uparrow .</math>

== Confusion with nimbers ==
The only [[nimber]] confused with <math>\uparrow</math> is <math>*</math>. This is easily illustrated by the Hackenbush example, as a blue delphinium and a green edge along with a <math>*2</math> position is not [[Fuzzy game|fuzzy]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />
